newsitem.title: USA: GOLF-BRISKY, KANADA SHARE LEAD AT DEPOSIT GUARANTY CLASSIC.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-BRISKY, KANADA SHARE LEAD AT DEPOSIT GUARANTY CLASSIC.

text.p: Americans Mike Brisky and Craig Kanada, non-winners on the PGA Tour, shot first-round scores of eight-under-par 64 Thursday to share the lead in the $1 million Deposit Guaranty Golf Classic.
Damp, soft greens, which allowed players to shoot for the pins like throwing darts at a dartboard, made for low scores at the Jack Nicklaus-designed Annandale Golf Club.
Don Pooley and J.P. Hayes both shot 65, and seven players shot 66. David Toms, who won the Quad City Classic for his first PGA Tour victory last week, led a group of 12 more players who shot 67.
One hundred of the 154 contestants broke par.
Defending champion Willie Wood shot 68, as did Canadian Richard Zokol and Sweden's Gabriel Hjertstedt.
Kanada, a tour rookie who had never led a PGA Tournament before Thursday, made an eagle on the par-five 18th hole when he reached the green with a driver and a four-wood and then sank a 10-foot putt.
"I'm a rookie so I'm learning," Kanada said. "In Memphis I shot a first-round 66 and then followed with a 77. Most of your learning comes from bad experience."
Brisky, who had three top 10 finishes on the tour in 1996, said he "put it all together" for the first time in four months. He birdied seven of 10 holes during one stretch.

"I played much better than I've been playing today," Brisky said. "It feels good to play good again. The greens here are so soft you can shoot right at them. I actually hit a three-wood into one green and the ball backed up six inches."
Players here are shooting for a first prize of $180,000. The field will be cut to the low 70 scorers and ties following Friday's second round, which might be threatened by tropical storm Daniel.
